$comment: Fixture catalog for the structured Factur-X/EN16931 Phase 1 path. All data is fictional ('Unternehmen X' as buyer, 'Beispiel Lieferant GmbH' as seller, synthetic addresses/VAT IDs/IBANs) -- see docs/invoice_phase1/test_matrix.md and organization_master_data.py. Each entry's 'verifiedBy' points at the pytest test(s) that actually run the fixture through the public Phase 1 endpoints and assert on the real response -- this file documents intent, the tests are the machine-readable source of truth for expected results.

fixtures.purpose: Baseline valid EN16931 invoice, submitted both as direct XML and (embedded via generate_from_binary, see conftest.py's valid_hybrid_pdf_bytes fixture) as a hybrid Factur-X PDF.
fixtures.path: direct XML: hybrid_pdf/xml source_type -> XSD (1.09) -> Schematron (1.09) -> normalize -> content controls -> ORG-001 -> aggregate
fixtures.explanation: Every field present, buyer matches the built-in Unternehmen X master-data snapshot exactly, totals reconcile, no document-level charges/allowances/prepayment.

fixtures.path: xml source_type -> XSD (1.09) fails -> Schematron not run (BLOCKED_BY_XSD_INVALID) -> aggregate
fixtures.explanation: A field violates the XSD type system (a decimal-typed value holds a non-numeric string). Schematron rules assume XSD-valid input -- verified directly that running the official stylesheet against this exact fixture makes Saxon raise a dynamic type-conversion error (FORG0001) rather than a meaningful business-rule finding -- so it is deliberately not run once STR-003 has already failed.

fixtures.purpose: Required scenario: Schematron-invalid invoice with retained rule ID.
fixtures.path: xml source_type -> XSD (1.09) passes -> Schematron (1.09) fails -> aggregate
fixtures.explanation: SellerTradeParty has no SpecifiedTaxRegistration at all (no VAT ID, no legal registration ID) -- XSD-legal (the element is optional in the schema) but violates BR-CO-26 (a Seller identifier of some kind is mandatory) and, through the same missing identifier, BR-S-02 for the standard-rated line. Each finding carries the real official rule ID, the human-readable BR-* text, and a precise XPath location, generated by the vendored, hash-verified official stylesheet itself -- not fabricated by this codebase.

fixtures.path: xml source_type -> XSD (1.09) passes -> Schematron (1.09) fails -> DigiTax CAL-003 also fails -> aggregate
fixtures.explanation: grossAmount = taxBasis + taxAmount is correct (119.00), but payableAmount (125.00) does not equal grossAmount - prepaidAmount + roundingAmount (119.01) -- isolates the failure to the payable-amount reconciliation step (BR-CO-16) specifically, distinct from a gross-amount mismatch. Caught independently by two different mechanisms: the DigiTax CAL-003 business control (formula/expected/actual/difference in `details`) and the official EN16931 Schematron rule (STR-004, rule FX-SCH-A-000122, same BR-CO-16 text) -- deliberately kept as two separate findings rather than deduplicated, since they come from independently-reviewed logic (this codebase's own arithmetic vs. the vendored official stylesheet) and agreeing is itself useful evidence.

fixtures.purpose: Required scenario: unsupported but recognizable profile.
fixtures.path: xml source_type -> DOC-001 fails before extraction/XSD/Schematron ever run
fixtures.explanation: A genuinely valid Factur-X MINIMUM-profile document -- recognized as Factur-X (not UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT, which is reserved for formats not recognized as Factur-X at all, e.g. XRechnung), but only EN16931 is processable by the reviewed starter control profile so far (see /capabilities' recognizedLevels vs. processableLevels).

fixtures.purpose: Required scenario: hybrid PDF without an accepted embedded XML file.
fixtures.path: PDF with an XML attachment under an unrecognized filename -> document_intake.py's filename allowlist rejects it -> falls back to plain_pdf (mock OCR/PDF) path, not hybrid_pdf
fixtures.expectedStatus: unauffaellig (via the PDF/mock-adapter path; this fixture tests classification, not a specific control finding)
fixtures.explanation: The attached XML is a genuinely valid EN16931 invoice, but under a filename that is not one of the well-known Factur-X/ZUGFeRD/Order-X attachment names (facturx.ALL_FILENAMES). Proves the PDF is safely downgraded to plain_pdf because of the filename allowlist alone, not silently parsed as structured data via a filename-guessing fallback (a real vulnerability class this codebase deliberately closed -- see document_intake.py's module docstring).

fixtures.purpose: Regression: a valid invoice with no TotalPrepaidAmount element at all (BT-113 is optional per EN16931/CII) must not fail CAL-003 outright.
fixtures.explanation: Not one of the 6 required scenarios, but kept from the prior review round -- confidently-absent optional amounts must be treated as 0, not a missing-field failure.

fixtures.purpose: Regression: BT-114 (roundingAmount) belongs in the payable-amount reconciliation, not the gross-amount one.
fixtures.explanation: Not one of the 6 required scenarios, but kept from the prior review round.
